derivation: Each value is an exact Decimal derivation from cited source facts (the quotes in submissions.json) by the conventions in 'arithmetic'; nothing is read from code under test. Gap cells are spelled with the product's gap spelling; G# is bound at run time.

cell_notation.num: amount is the exact stored Decimal string; unit is the Fact unit; decimals is Fact.decimals; shown is the product spelling (display.py _number, report_view.fact_spelling): decimal_fraction shows amount x 100 to `decimals` places half-up with a percent sign; basis_points, years and days show the exact stored amount and ' bp', ' years', ' days'
cell_notation.gap: status missing -> shown '∅ G#'; status not_applicable -> shown '∅ G# n.m.'; G# is bound at run time (an A7-style exception)
cell_notation.value_class: source (quoted level or term), calculated (Python), analyst_judgment (recovery and technicals)
cell_notation.calculated_cites: a calculated fact carries the page-level cites of its inputs

arithmetic.decimal_context: 28 significant digits, ROUND_HALF_EVEN for division and exp; stored outputs are quantised ROUND_HALF_UP and are never the input of a later step (every output derives from unrounded intermediates)
arithmetic.price_unit: levels are quoted as a percentage of par; stored as decimal_fraction (98.50 -> 0.9850)
arithmetic.day_count: Act/365 Fixed from the quotation date (as_of of bid and offer, which must be equal) to the final maturity date: days = maturity - quotation date; years = days / 365; years is stored quantised to 0.01 for display only: every later step (discount, margin, intensity, probability) uses the unrounded days / 365 (3.98 shown, 3.9780821917808... used; with 3.98 the offer margin would be 18.8 bp, not 18.9)
arithmetic.annualised_discount_bp: (100 - price) / years x 100 basis points per annum, price in points of par; stored quantised to 0.1 bp
arithmetic.simple_discount_margin_bp: contractual margin (bp, cited) + annualised discount; requires a cited zero amortisation; floor ignored (a floor on the reference rate does not enter a margin); stored quantised to 0.1 bp. Convention: the discounted-spread form of the loan market, margin + (100 - price) / years, NOT divided by price (dividing gives 38.3/28.6/19.0 bp at bid/mid/offer) and NOT the market's three-year-life convention (remaining life to final maturity is used instead); Act/365 Fixed; settlement taken as the quotation date (a settlement lag of about a week is ignored)
arithmetic.reference_rate: all-in yield (simple) = reference rate level + simple discount margin / 10000; the reference rate level must be quoted ({quote, percent_text}, percent_text a whole token once in its own verbatim quote) and is absent from every frozen source, so the yield is Not calculable in every pack case; fixture_with_benchmark exercises the pure function with a test vector, and the builder composes a throwaway quoted level to exercise the yield cells, claim and validator (nothing of it is written out)
arithmetic.annual_default_intensity_bp: simple discount margin / (1 - recovery) (credit triangle: the whole spread is default compensation), stored quantised to 0.1 bp; needs recovery in [0, 1) and a positive margin. A higher recovery raises the intensity for the same margin
arithmetic.cumulative_default_probability: 1 - exp(-(intensity / 10000) x years) with unrounded intensity and years, stored quantised to 0.0001 (shown to two places as a percent); risk-neutral
arithmetic.not_meaningful: a simple discount margin <= 0 gives status not_applicable for both default measures (shown n.m.), never 0
arithmetic.talk: indicative talk is shown and compared with the mid (context row) but enters no spread, yield or default figure; its period is the commentary publication date (page:2), not the quotation date
arithmetic.recovery: analyst input in percent (D11), 0 <= x < 100; the literal is 70 percent, the first-lien loan CDS convention (the frozen financial page:5 states a senior secured term loan; the senior-unsecured CDS convention would be 40 percent). The convention is the analyst's knowledge: no source states it and it is not verified against one. At 40 percent the mid margin 28.3 bp would give 47.1 bp and 1.86 percent. Stored decimal_fraction decimals 0; an uncited analyst_judgment fact: it has no citation or calculation id so a claim cannot reference it as a figure
